chapter_title: What is Virginal; or, otherwise, what is Continent
spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation: On the Virginal and the Continent

---

**¶1:**
What is the state of wisdom that is called "pristine"? Or the [GAP-1: state of wisdom that] is called "restored" — what is it? By what principle is pristine wisdom recognized as such? And restored wisdom, which is given this name — by what principle is it known as "restored"?

---

**¶3:**
What is called "pristine" belongs to the mystery of the infinite degrees of Divine order. It is called "pristine" by virtue of all the wisdom that never [GAP-2: underwent] spiritual death, nor descended into the conflict that falsity wages against good.

---

**¶4:**
However, what is called "restored" pertains to the mystery of the wisdom that descended and became intermingled with falsity. It was defiled in corporeal and sensory states [GAP-3: through its captivity in external nature] and yet ascended again toward its celestial origin. [GAP-4: Therefore they] called it "restored."

---

**¶5:**
Furthermore, the holy pristine wisdoms [GAP-5: are of such a nature that even if] they should go forth against the [GAP-6: assault of falsity, they would] not undergo spiritual death, nor [GAP-7: suffer contamination from evil].

---

**¶6:**
On the other hand, what is called "restored" is that wisdom which became intermingled with falsity, was purified, ascended out of all created and sensory states, and was confirmed in the Divine order. It is called "restored" because it tasted of self-love and concupiscence; but afterward it was cleansed from these and [GAP-8: became a] holy state of good.

---

**¶7:**
Furthermore, what is called "pristine" is that wisdom which was purified by the manifestation of the Divine Truth sent forth into the world. It ascended and attained [GAP-9: the] interior celestial states. It was confirmed in the forms of Divine good and truth.

---

**¶8:**
Again, what is [GAP-10: called] "restored" is the remaining portion of that wisdom which was left behind after what had been purified ascended. It rises and descends through successive states of reformation. Also, there is a portion [GAP-11: of] it that enters into and assumes the condition of the natural and corporeal person. Again, even that portion shall be chosen while still in the natural state, [GAP-12: receive] the interior hope of salvation, and become a holy state of good. And they name it "restored."

---

**¶9:**
Furthermore, what is named "pristine" is the Divine influx of interior understanding when it descends and takes on the interior forms [GAP-13: of] those who are in genuine good. However, on the other hand, what is called "restored" is the regenerate will, when it has been purified from the old proprium — the inherited and accumulated selfhood. It is cleansed and strips off the evil that was compounded with it, and it becomes a restored state of holiness.

---

**¶10:**
And also, what is called "pristine" in the natural person is the state of one who has never conjoined his understanding with the love of self and the world, and has not been defiled by that conjunction. However, in contrast, what is called "restored" is the state of one who was conjoined with worldly affection and natural desire. Afterward, he purifies himself from that affection [GAP-14: and] renounces it entirely. And because of this he [GAP-15: is separated from falsity] and becomes a holy and restored one.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: What is the virgin that is named 'virginal'? Or the [one that] is called 'continent', what is it? Or by what category is the [vi]rgin called 'virginal'? Or [the co]ntinent, which is given this name, by what category is it named '[c]ontinent'?

What is called 'virginal' is assigned to the mystery of the aeons of greatness. And they called it 'virginal' by the category of all the light that did not [taste] of death, nor come to the enemy's war.

However, what is called 'continent' occurs to the mystery of the light that came and was mixed with the darkness. It was defiled in bodies [of the creatures] and went up to the light. [They] called [it 'co]ntinent'.
Furthermore, the holy vir[gin]als [are of such a nature that, even] should they come out against the en[emy and come to the war, they would not] taste death, nor [be defiled].

On the other hand, what is called 'continent' [is this li]ght that mixed with the darkness, was purif[ie]d, came [up f]rom all the creatures, and was confirmed in the great[ness]. They called it 'continent' since it tasted [of the l]ust; but afterwards was cleansed from it and [become an] holy one.
Furthermore, what is called ['vi]rginal' is this light that was purified by the ima[ge] of the [A]mbassador. It wen[t up and] attained [the] he[ights. It was] confirmed in the image of the gods.

Again, what is [called] 'continent' is the remainder of this light th[at] remained behind, from what was cleansed. It goes up and comes down in transmigration. Al[so], there is a part [of] it that shall come and attain the form of [hum]an [fl]esh. Again, that one too shall be chosen in the flesh, [accept] the hope, and become an holy one. And they name it 'continent'.

Furthermore, what is named 'virginal' is the Light Mind, should he come and assume the images [of] the ele[ct]. However, on the other hand, what is called 'contin[ent]' is the new man, should it be purified from this old man. And it is cleansed and strips off the Sin that is compounded with it, and it becomes a continent one.

And also, what is called 'virgi[n]al' in the flesh, is a man if he has [ne]ver joined himself to woman, has not been defiled by intercourse. However, [i]n contrast, what is called 'continent', is the man who has a wom[a]n in the world. Afterwards, he cleanses himself from her [and] renounces her. And because of this he [is purified] and he becomes an holy contin[en]t one.

fills.explanation: The parallel structure requires a pronoun phrase referring to the second category ("the continent"), and "one that" naturally pairs with "the virgin that is named 'virginal'" in the preceding clause.
"Taste of death" is a standard Manichaean and Semitic idiom for undergoing spiritual death, and the same phrase recurs in ¶5, confirming this vocabulary.

The spiritual reading indicates captivity in external nature; ¶6's parallel "came up from all the creatures" confirms that "creatures" is the Kephalaia's natural-plane term for the external states in which the light was bound.
The impersonal "They called it" formula is the chapter's standard naming construction, used identically in ¶3, ¶6, and ¶8.

fills.fill: are of such a nature that, even
fills.explanation: The spiritual reading specifies "are of such a nature that even if," and the text needs a predicate for "the holy virginals" that sets up the conditional "should they come out against the enemy"; "even should they come out" is a natural conditional construction.

fills.fill: emy and come to the war, they would not
fills.explanation: The phrase "come to the enemy's war" appears in ¶3 as the parallel description of virginal light; here the conditional form completes the sentence before "taste death," and "they would not" provides the necessary negation.

The spiritual reading indicates "suffer contamination from evil"; "defiled" is the chapter's consistent term for contamination by darkness (used in ¶4, ¶6, ¶10), and "nor be defiled" parallels "not taste death" as the second negative consequence the virginals are immune to.

The editor's "become an" fits: the same construction "become an holy one" appears in ¶8 and ¶10, establishing it as a fixed formula in the chapter, and the bare infinitive after "and" is consistent with the translator's style throughout.
The definite article "the" is required before "heights" as the standard construction for attaining a specific celestial location in Kephalaia cosmology.
The formulaic phrase "what is called 'continent'" is used identically in ¶4, ¶6, and ¶9, making "called" the only contextually appropriate word.
The partitive construction "a part of it" is standard for describing a portion of the light that remains behind, and the preposition "of" is grammatically required.

The spiritual reading gives "receive," and "accept" is its natural-register equivalent in the Kephalaia for actively taking on the hope of salvation; the editor's choice fits the context of being chosen and receiving the interior hope.
The preposition "of" is required in the construction "the images of the elect," connecting the Light Mind's assumed forms to the elect who receive it.
The conjunction "and" connects the two parallel actions of purification — cleansing himself from her and renouncing her — as a coordinated pair describing the process of separation.

The spiritual reading indicates "is separated from falsity"; in the Kephalaia's natural register, "is purified" is the chapter's standard term for the result of cleansing and renunciation (paralleling ¶6's "was purified" and ¶4's pattern of defilement-then-purification), and it provides the causal result introduced by "because of this."
